note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  - Acute chest tightness for ~3 hours. Preceded by an upper respiratory infection/cold last week.
  - Patient reports he ran out of his inhaled steroid (Clenil Modulite) and salbutamol (Ventolin) ~1 week ago while away at university.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  - Onset: ~3 hours prior to consultation.
  - Symptoms: persistent chest tightness, mild shortness of breath (worse with exertion/stairs, not at rest), wheeze and non-productive cough. Slightly worse at night historically.
  - No improvement since onset.
- ENT-relevant symptoms:
  - Throat: recent sore throat during last week's cold; no current throat closing sensation reported.
  - Voice/hoarseness: not reported.
  - Dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling: not reported.
  - Nasal/ocular: runny nose during recent cold; history of hayfever and dust allergy.
  - Stridor/noisy breathing: wheeze reported, no stridor described.
  - Dyspnea: mild; not short of breath at rest, worse on exertion.
  - Facial/lip/tongue/uvula swelling: none reported.
  - Ear/neck: had sore throat/runny nose last week; no ongoing ear pain or neck swelling reported.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  - Asthma since childhood. Severe exacerbation in adolescence (age ~16–17) requiring hospital admission and intubation.
  - Uses salbutamol (Ventolin) and inhaled steroid Clenil Modulite chronically but has been without both for ~1 week.
- Allergies and current medications:
  - Drug allergies: none reported.
  - Other allergies: hayfever; dust allergy; childhood milk protein allergy.
  - Current medications: Salbutamol (Ventolin) — dose/route/frequency not documented; Clenil Modulite (inhaled steroid) — dose/route/frequency not documented. Patient currently out of these medications.
  - Prior injections/auto-injector: not documented.
- Social/context:
  - University student; was away from home last week.
  - Accompaniment/supervision during consultation: not documented.

Objective:
- Observable swelling/distribution: none stated.
- Airway/breathing descriptors:
  - Patient reports audible wheeze and mild shortness of breath; not breathless at rest; more breathless on stairs.
- Mental status/associated features:
  - Patient anxious/concerned about recurrence of prior severe asthma requiring intubation.
  - No dizziness, syncope, or altered consciousness reported.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded.
- Presence of another person with the patient: Not recorded.

Assessment:
- Working clinical impression:
  - Acute asthma exacerbation, likely precipitated by recent viral upper respiratory infection and omission of regular inhaled steroid and short-acting bronchodilator.
- Evidence summary from transcript:
  - Known asthma with prior severe exacerbation requiring intubation.
  - Acute onset chest tightness, wheeze and non-productive cough after recent cold.
  - Has been without inhaled steroid and salbutamol for ~1 week.
  - Symptoms mild-moderate by history (not breathless at rest; ambulatory).
- Differential diagnosis from provided DDx (top items aligning with transcript):
  1) Acute asthma exacerbation (High likelihood)
     - Justification: established asthma, wheeze, chest tightness, precipitated by recent URTI and missed inhaler therapy.
     - Opposing evidence: patient not short of breath at rest; no objective measures (PEF, SpO2) available to confirm severity.
  2) Viral bronchitis / post-viral wheeze (Medium likelihood)
     - Justification: recent cold last week with persistent cough and wheeze; could represent post-viral airway hyperreactivity.
     - Opposing evidence: strong pre-existing asthma and missed preventive/rescue inhalers make primary asthma exacerbation more likely.
- Conflict noted: None between transcript and DDx content (DDx consistent with history).

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised (per transcript):
  - Prescribe inhaled medications: salbutamol (Ventolin) and inhaled steroid (Clenil Modulite) — prescription to be sent (doctor stated within the hour). Dose/administration details not documented in transcript.
  - Prescribe oral corticosteroid tablets for 5 days: "two tablets in the morning" (as advised by clinician in transcript). Specific steroid name/dose not documented.
  - Provide a spacer device and instructions for use (prescription/supply to be sent).
  - Advice: use Ventolin as needed; if using Ventolin more frequently than every 3 hours, seek medical attention.
- Specific patient instructions:
  - Rest and avoid strenuous exertion until symptoms improve.
  - Use inhaled steroid regularly as prescribed and salbutamol PRN for wheeze.
  - Follow spacer instructions to improve inhaler delivery if available.
  - Obtain and commence prescribed oral steroid course as directed.
  - Time off work: clinician advised possible time off; patient may self-certify for first seven days.
- Escalation criteria / red flags (seek urgent care or call emergency services):
  - Worsening shortness of breath at rest.
  - Increasing work of breathing, inability to speak full sentences, accessory muscle use.
  - New or progressive throat closing sensation, stridor, hoarseness, drooling, or facial/tongue swelling.
  - Chest pain, syncope, light-headedness, or marked deterioration in mental status.
  - Need to use salbutamol more frequently than every 3 hours or poor response to medication.
- Follow-up:
  - If symptoms do not improve or worsen, seek same-day medical review or go to ED.
  - Primary care/respiratory follow-up recommended for asthma review, inhaler technique and controller therapy adherence (not specifically arranged in transcript).
  - Consider formal peak flow measurement or pulse oximetry assessment if available at follow-up.
- Auto-injector and allergy clinic:
  - No discussion of epinephrine auto-injector or allergy referral documented; not applicable based on available history.
- COVID-19 vaccine suitability: Not discussed.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (respiratory rate, heart rate, oxygen saturation, blood pressure, temperature).
  - Objective exam findings (auscultation, peak expiratory flow measurement).
  - Exact names/doses/routes/frequencies of prescribed inhalers and oral steroid tablet (steroid name and mg not documented).
  - Smoking status.
  - Presence/availability of spacer at home and exact spacer type.
  - Documentation of prior anaphylaxis plan or epinephrine auto-injector (if relevant).
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx:
  - None identified; DDx aligns with transcript-based assessment (conflict noted: none).
- Transcript quality comment:
  - Audio had intermittent cutting in/out in places; some short sections were inaudible but overall history and management decisions were adequately captured.
